title: fix: session maintenance delays other Gateway requests
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: automatic session maintenance delays other Gateway requests when a large session inventory has no entries eligible for cleanup.

## User Impact

Routine session writes avoid repeatedly reading the entire protection-key inventory when maintenance has no age or cap candidates. Active work, parent sessions, lifecycle operations, retention rules, and writer ordering keep their existing behavior. No configuration change, migration, or schema change is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared planner now obtains its protection set once, immediately before its first phase with candidates. This includes cap-only cleanup after an empty age scan. SQLite retains the same synchronous transaction and ownership checks; legacy, preview, and file-backed callers retain their prepared protection sets.

## Evidence

The new no-work regression fails on the original code with 96 unnecessary projected rows across three ordinary writes and passes with zero. Both cap-only and age-plus-cap cases retain active-admission, lifecycle, provider, active-key, and parent protection. All 107 focused tests passed, covering maintenance, legacy read/write parity, cleanup previews, pruning, cap archives, stale handles, and write-triggered maintenance. The full build and all changed-source checks passed for the profiled maintenance commit. Fresh independent Codex review through P2 found no actionable issues in the final combined diff.

A serial baseline/candidate/candidate/baseline measurement used byte-identical closed databases with 3,550 rich session entries, eight active admissions, eight warmups, and 60 measured maintenance transactions per cell. Mean transaction wall time fell from 10.65 to 1.53 ms, and CPU from 10.94 to 1.60 ms (85.4% less). Every canonical database row remained unchanged.

A separate paired Gateway run used the same synthetic fixture and fixed workload: 16 turns, 64 history reads, 64 updates, and 16 rounds of list, readiness, Control UI, and subscription probes. Both runs completed all requests without failures and exited cleanly.

| Gateway measurement | Baseline | Candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Main-thread CPU during timed load | 6,210 ms | 5,323 ms (-14.3%) |
| Timed load duration | 6,350 ms | 5,480 ms (-13.7%) |
| History p50 / p95 | 99 / 673 ms | 58 / 466 ms |
| Session update p50 / p95 | 42 / 153 ms | 27 / 146 ms |
| Session list p50 / maximum (16 samples) | 45 / 295 ms | 48 / 161 ms |

Maintenance writer execution fell from 1,269 ms across 60 admissions to 251 ms across 66 admissions. Foreground request counts match; asynchronous background work can vary. Other results were mixed: readiness p50 rose from 9 to 16 ms, and entry-patch summed queue wait rose from 4,199 to 4,391 ms with 151 versus 147 patches. This single paired run is a point measurement, not a claim that all queueing or latency is fixed.

Baseline source: `7cf2696575cb604a8afa02af5187a65834f5b63e`; candidate: `adc29616e0816039ab4a9ece0ba65ceb049bdad4`. These are isolated synthetic measurements, not deployed latency claims. The raw readiness delay can retain profiler-start overhead, and the mock request total includes setup; neither is used as an in-load CPU measurement.

## CI Repair

The first CI run exposed an unrelated failure introduced on main by #148195: the new wizard recovery integration test ran in a worker thread, but its pending-install migration requires the host-owned SQLite broker. It reproduces unchanged on main with the same assertion failure. This PR adds that test to the existing forked database-consumer routing list, preserving production code, authority checks, and assertions. The exact test, setup-flow and install-rollback siblings, and routing checks pass: 170 focused cases, plus the tooling changed-source checks.

The branch was refreshed onto `bfaac101391ec82d66aa443c589f580cc82bf656` for this CI repair. All seven maintenance files remain byte-identical to the profiled candidate above; the final head is `3eda1981dceb08ad7cd09263d36c010930d3884c`.
